characters.name: Harlan 'Sparky' Vance (via Remote DRM-9 Fault Logger)

characters.signature_quote: KZ9-Omega automated fault log: the #4 Belt-Master marzelvane bushing is wobbling four-point-eight degrees, the oil capacitor is ruptured, and we are splattering sixty kilohertz across the whole forty-one-meter band. Do not send further citations.
characters.bio: Monitors unstaffed Meridian Plateau Trunk Hop #1 via its tower-mounted inspection camera during a six-week planetary silicate dust storm while waiting for replacement filter capacitors impounded at Quarantine Buoy 12.
characters.language_sample_transcript: This is Chief Engineer Harlon Vance at Meridian Relay KZ9-Omega on seventy-one-forty. Do not cite us for sixty-kilohertz splatter! We are in a Force-Nine silicate dust storm, the marzelvane bushings are wobbling four point eight degrees, and Tower One just took a sixty-kilovolt arc!
characters.phonetic_and_conlang_notes: Corporate High-Voltage Switchgear Jargon ('marzelvane bushings', 'sixty-kilohertz splatter', 'ceramic standoff').

worldbuilding.habitat_and_culture: The Meridian Silicate Plateau on planet Aurelia-IV is a vast, unstaffed desert plain where boiling ochre dust storms generate 60-kilovolt triboelectric potentials across exposed antenna steelwork. The only camera on site is bolted high up on the main relay tower looking down across its ceramic feedline insulators.
worldbuilding.spectrum_gimmick_title: 50 kW Capacitor Rupture Splattering ±30 kHz (WTWW / Radio Havana Windhowl Homage)
worldbuilding.hauser_commentary: Automated Relay KZ9-Omega on 7140—cited by the Spectrum Bureau for coming on early and splattering a 60-kHz-wide signal from 7110 to 7170 because of a ruptured capacitor and a 60 kV dust squall arcing across the tower's ceramic insulators. Mostly S9+40 of dead-air silicate windhowl.
worldbuilding.qsl_postcard_style: Corporate Hardware Underwriter & Tower-Cam Telemetry Card (Van Allen Switchgear)
worldbuilding.qsl_animation_notes: Seen from the high mast-mounted inspection camera on Tower #1: a blinding 60 kV cyan plasma arc leaps from the parabolic dish below right into the foreground ceramic insulator with a shower of sparks and a red 'NOV CITED: ±30 kHz SPLATTER' stamp!

discovery_arc.summary: Cited for 60 kHz bandwidth splatter and +4.8° marzelvane bushing wobble as tower-cam captures 60 kV arcs hitting the foreground insulator.
Directional night-pattern phaser fails completely, accidentally beaming internal Syndicate customs audio 42,000 AU backward into GOR-9's lap.
